tasks.title: Create ngv2/sourcing/huntr_client.py: deterministic /bounties poller behind injected fetcher seam
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/sourcing/huntr_client.py exists with EXACTLY the verbatim content from the brief's Deliverables block (byte-for-byte).
Module is importable as ngv2.sourcing.huntr_client via namespace-package resolution (no ngv2/sourcing/__init__.py is added).
The only network edge (urllib GET) lives in make_url_fetcher(); all other functions accept an injected fetcher and never touch the network.

fetch_raw performs ETag conditional requests (304 + cached_body reuses cache), bounded exponential-backoff retry on 429/5xx via injected sleep, calls injected rate_limiter(host) before each attempt, and raises FetchError when retries are exhausted.
parse_feed tolerantly parses JSON into {repos, formats}; feed_to_bounties yields typed ngv2.contracts.Bounty records with eligible taken straight from the feed entry, ordered by repo name.
No edits to ngv2.bounty_gate, ngv2.huntr_data, or ngv2.contracts; no LLM/randomness/subprocess used.
tasks.verification_command: cd /home/xnihil0zer0/NobleGreedv2 && .venv/bin/python -c "import ngv2.sourcing.huntr_client as m; print(m.fetch_bounties, m.fetch_raw, m.parse_feed, m.feed_to_bounties, m.make_url_fetcher, m.FetchError)"

spec.objective: Build the new io_adapter module ngv2/sourcing/huntr_client.py that deterministically fetches huntr's /bounties feed (behind an injected fetcher seam) and parses it into the {repos, formats} shape consumed by ngv2.bounty_gate.gate and ngv2.huntr_data.parse_bounties, yielding typed ngv2.contracts.Bounty records.
functional_requirements: Define Fetcher = (url, headers) -> (status:int, body:str, resp_headers:dict), RateLimiter = (host) -> None, and Sleeper = (seconds) -> None type aliases, plus module constants DEFAULT_BASE_URL='https://huntr.com', BOUNTIES_PATH='/bounties', MAX_RETRIES=4, BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS=1.0, RETRY_STATUS={429,500,502,503,504}, and a FetchError(RuntimeError).

make_url_fetcher() returns the production fetcher seam backed by urllib.request, decoding the body as utf-8/'replace' and mapping urllib HTTPError into (code, '', headers) so it conforms to the Fetcher signature.
_host_of(url) extracts the host portion of a URL for per-host rate limiting.

fetch_raw(url, *, fetcher, rate_limiter=None, sleep=None, etag=None, cached_body=None, max_retries=MAX_RETRIES, backoff_base=BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS) sends Accept/User-Agent headers, adds If-None-Match when etag is set, and returns (body, etag).

fetch_raw calls rate_limiter(host) before each attempt (when provided), reuses cached_body on 304, returns body plus the response ETag on 200, retries 429/5xx with backoff_base * 2**attempt via the injected sleep, raises FetchError immediately on other non-2xx statuses, and raises FetchError once retries are exhausted.

parse_feed(body) tolerantly json-loads the body, accepting the canonical {'repos':{...},'formats':{...}} object or a bare list / embedded 'bounties' list of records folded into repos via _repo_entry, defaulting missing sections to {} and never raising on a well-formed-but-sparse feed.
_repo_entry(rec) folds a flat bounty record into a repo entry with eligible (default True), tier, observed_payouts, max_paid, submissions normalized to the bounty-gate shape.

feed_to_bounties(feed, *, platform='huntr', discovered_at='') converts the parsed feed into deterministically repo-name-sorted typed ngv2.contracts.Bounty records, deriving observed_payout from the first positive critical/high/medium/low payout and taking eligible straight from the feed entry.

fetch_bounties(*, fetcher, base_url=DEFAULT_BASE_URL, rate_limiter=None, sleep=None, etag=None, cached_body=None, discovered_at='') composes fetch_raw -> parse_feed -> feed_to_bounties and returns (feed, bounties, etag).
spec.interfaces: Exposes fetch_bounties(*, fetcher, base_url='https://huntr.com', rate_limiter=None, sleep=None, etag=None, cached_body=None, discovered_at='') -> (feed, list[Bounty], etag); fetch_raw(url, *, fetcher, rate_limiter=None, sleep=None, etag=None, cached_body=None, max_retries=MAX_RETRIES, backoff_base=BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS) -> (body, etag); parse_feed(body) -> {repos, formats}; feed_to_bounties(feed, *, platform='huntr', discovered_at='') -> list[Bounty]; make_url_fetcher() -> Fetcher; FetchError. Output feed shape: feed['repos'][owner/repo] = {eligible, tier, observed_payouts, max_paid, submissions} and feed['formats'].
edge_cases: 304 status with cached_body returns the cached body and the original etag; 304 with no cached_body falls through (not a 200 / not retryable -> FetchError).
Empty or invalid JSON body parses to {repos:{}, formats:{}} without raising.
Feed with a bare list or embedded 'bounties' list folds records into repos via _repo_entry without clobbering an existing repos entry (setdefault).
All attempts return a retryable status -> FetchError reporting exhausted retries and last status; rate_limiter invoked once per attempt.
Non-retryable non-2xx (e.g. 404) raises FetchError on the first attempt.

Bounty.validate() invariants are respected: platform/repo_url/package/cwe non-empty (cwe defaults to CWE-94, repo_url built from repo, package from repo tail), payouts/submissions non-negative, fp_risk in [0,1].
non_goals: No real network call in any path the oracle exercises; the fetcher is injected.
No brittle HTML parsing; only tolerant JSON parsing of the feed.
Do not change ngv2.bounty_gate, ngv2.huntr_data, or ngv2.contracts.
Do not qualify, rank, clone, scan, or submit bounties.
No LLM, randomness, or subprocess use; add no separate __init__.py.
spec.implementation_notes:
Emit the file VERBATIM exactly as given in the brief's Deliverables block. The full content (header docstring through fetch_bounties) is reproduced byte-for-byte in the brief; do not add, reorder, or reword anything. The module is a single new file at ngv2/sourcing/huntr_client.py importable as ngv2.sourcing.huntr_client through Python namespace-package resolution -- do NOT create ngv2/sourcing/__init__.py. It imports only json, typing, and ngv2.contracts.Bounty (urllib is imported lazily inside make_url_fetcher). Preserve legacy's load-bearing insight that /bounties is authoritative for paid eligibility (Bounty.eligible comes straight from the feed entry). Touch no other module.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: An in-memory canned fetcher returning scripted (status, body, headers) tuples per attempt (including a 429-then-200 sequence and an always-429 sequence), a counting rate_limiter and recording sleep stub, a canonical {repos, formats} JSON body, a bare-list/embedded-bounties JSON body, and an ETag header for the 200 response.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is verbatim emission of a fixed file, so it is low-risk to write but must be reproduced exactly; tests carry the verification weight.

spec.objective: Write the hermetic, committed oracle tests/test_huntr_client_wired.py that exercises ngv2.sourcing.huntr_client end to end through injected seams, asserting the parsed output, the resilience behaviors, and downstream consumability.
functional_requirements: Provide an in-memory fetcher seam that returns scripted (status, body, resp_headers) tuples and never performs real I/O; assert fetch_bounties returns the {repos, formats} feed, a typed list[Bounty], and the response ETag.
Assert that on a 429-then-200 sequence fetch_raw retries with exponential backoff via the injected sleep (recorded delays) and calls the injected per-host rate_limiter before each attempt.
Assert ETag conditional behavior: a 304 response with cached_body reuses the cached body and preserves the etag, and that If-None-Match is sent when an etag is supplied.
Assert FetchError is raised when retries are exhausted (always-429) and on a non-retryable non-2xx status (e.g. 404).

Assert parse_feed tolerance (canonical object, bare list, embedded 'bounties' list) and that feed_to_bounties emits repo-name-sorted Bounty records whose eligible is taken straight from the feed entry and that pass Bounty.validate().
Assert the emitted feed is consumed without error by ngv2.bounty_gate.gate(owner_repo, cwe, severity, bounties=feed) and ngv2.huntr_data.parse_bounties(feed).
spec.interfaces: Imports ngv2.sourcing.huntr_client (fetch_bounties, fetch_raw, parse_feed, feed_to_bounties, FetchError), ngv2.contracts.Bounty, ngv2.bounty_gate, ngv2.huntr_data. Test-local stubs: canned fetcher callable, counting rate_limiter, recording sleep.
edge_cases: Always-429 fetcher exhausts MAX_RETRIES and raises FetchError with last status reported.
304 with no cached_body must not silently succeed.
Empty/invalid JSON body parses to empty repos/formats without raising.
Mutation in mutation_target (ngv2.sourcing.huntr_client) must make at least one authored test FAIL (non-vacuity).
non_goals: No real network calls; do not hit huntr.com.
Do not modify the module under test or its neighbors from the test file.
spec.implementation_notes: Use only the public seams (injected fetcher/rate_limiter/sleep) -- never monkeypatch urllib. Build the canned fetcher as a closure over a list of scripted responses consumed per attempt. Keep the test deterministic (no randomness, no sleep wall-clock). The non-vacuity gate applies the declared mutant of ngv2.sourcing.huntr_client; ensure the retry/backoff and eligible-from-feed assertions are tight enough that a mutant fails.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Scripted response lists (429-then-200, always-429, 200-with-etag, 304-with-cache), a canonical {repos, formats} JSON fixture and a bare-list/embedded-bounties fixture, plus counting rate_limiter and recording sleep stubs.
